cards.title: CRO hypothesis structure: change, expected outcome, data-backed rationale
cards.claim: When creating a CRO hypothesis or AB test idea, the speaker says they look for three things: the change (what will be altered), the expected outcome (anticipated results), and the rationale, which must be backed by data/research.
cards.action: Define the test idea by stating what will be altered, the anticipated result, and the data-backed rationale for why the change is believed to affect the outcome.
applies_when: Creating a CRO hypothesis or AB test idea
Sufficient research/data analysis has been done to anticipate results
do_not_use_when: Expected outcome is set without enough research or data analysis to support it
unknowns: Not specified: exact minimum amount or type of research/data analysis required
Not specified: how to handle hypotheses when data is ambiguous
evidence_quotes: there are three things that we uh we always look for when we're creating a a hypothesis or AB test idea
Basically, one is the change. So, what is what do we plan to alter? Very simple. Two is the expected outcome.
And the rationale again, the data backs the rationale.

cards.title: AB test sample sizing and duration
cards.claim: For AB tests, the speaker says they would always run 50 to 100k sessions through a test; test duration should typically last from two to four weeks; for comprehensive tests on over 300,000 sessions, run for at least two weeks to avoid external factors altering the test; randomize the test.
cards.action: Run 50 to 100k sessions through an AB test; plan a two- to four-week duration; for comprehensive tests on stores over 300,000 sessions, run at least two weeks; randomize the test.
applies_when: Comprehensive testing on a store over 300,000 sessions
do_not_use_when: Multivariate testing at low volume (passage says multivariate testing should only be done at high volume)
unknowns: Not specified: whether 50–100k sessions is per variation or total test traffic
Not specified: exact statistical power threshold
Not specified: whether duration guidance changes for lower-volume stores beyond the over-300,000-session example
evidence_quotes: as far as sample sizing, we would always run 50 to 100k sessions through a test.
duration of test should typically last from two to four weeks.
We like to run especially on the comprehensive so over 300,000 sessions test for at least two weeks because we don't want external factors to alter the test.
obviously randomize that test as well.

cards.title: Prioritize CRO test ideas with PXL leaderboard scoring
cards.claim: The speaker says they use the PXL framework, put test ideas into a leaderboard, score each 1 to 10 on whether it is above the fold, noticeable in 5 seconds, and ease of implementation, then rank by highest score.
cards.action: After generating test ideas from data, enter them into a leaderboard, score each idea 1 to 10 on above-the-fold placement, 5-second noticeability, and ease of implementation, then rank by highest score and start with the highest-ranked ideas.
applies_when: Prioritizing CRO test ideas that come from data/research
do_not_use_when: Test ideas have not been generated from data/research
unknowns: Not specified: how to weight the three scoring criteria if they conflict
Not specified: exact score thresholds or tie-breaking rules
Not specified: whether the 1–10 scale applies to each criterion separately or as a combined score
evidence_quotes: We use the PXL framework. It's not ours. We're not going to pretend we invented it.
We'll put it into a leaderboard. So, when you have all your test ideas from that data, uh, you put the test ideas down here. You put a score of one to uh 1 to 10 here.
So, is it above the fold? Is it noticeable in 5 seconds? What's the ease of implementation? And then you rank it via the highest score.
